results.title: Overview | Crusoe Cloud
results.description: Crusoe Cloud offers three types of disks: Ephemeral Disks, Persistent Disks and Shared Disks. Ephemeral Disks are local to the virtual machine (on the same physical server). Persistent Disks are remote block storage volumes that are attached to a virtual machine.
snippets: Managed Kubernetes (CMK) — use Persistent and Shared Disks as PersistentVolumes via the Crusoe CSI driver.
Learn about Crusoe Cloud's disk types

Persistent Disks offer reasonable performance with high availability and durability. Persistent Disks have a lifecycle independent of any given virtual machine, and can be attached or detached while the VM is running or stopped.

Upon attaching a Shared Disk to one or more VMs, you can interface with the Shared Disk using standard NFS semantics. Like Persistent Disks, Shared Disks have a lifecycle independent of any given virtual machine, and can be attached or detached while the VM is running or stopped.

Changes to the "name" or "location" of the disk will force a re-creation of the disk (deletion and then creation of a new disk). Resizing a Persistent Disk changes the size of the underlying block device, but does not automatically grow the filesystem inside the VM.

From the console, select Storage > Disks in the left nav. Click Create Disk. Input a name for the disk, using only letters, numbers, - and _. Set the desired size of the disk from 1GiB to 10TiB. Set the desired block size of the disk—either 512B or 4096B. Click Create. Although Crusoe VMs come enabled with a 128 GB OS disk that is persistent, this disk is often not large enough for most AI or ML applications.

Enter the new size of the disk (disk size can only be increased). Click Confirm. To update an existing disk using the Crusoe Terraform provider, you can change the fields of an existing disk resource and run terraform apply.
